title: Flux Architecture IR
description: Component classes + attributes + actions, generalising Accelergy's plug-in pattern beyond energy to area/leakage/latency/thermal. See docs/ir.md. Amended by docs/decisions.md D1: covers full-SoC hierarchies (memory/compute/interconnect), not DNN-accelerator-only.

hierarchy.description: The top-level single-die/single-core memory+compute hierarchy. May be empty (docs/decisions.md D82) for a genuinely multi-core architecture whose real per-core hierarchies live inside interconnect.multi_core.cores[].architecture instead — the top-level shape doesn't apply once there's more than one independent compute array.

class.description: 'other' is the general-SoC escape hatch (D1) for components that aren't memory/compute/interconnect in the DNN-accelerator sense — e.g. protocol bridges, clock/power domains.

floorplan.description: Physical placement for thermal characterization (docs/decisions.md D64/D65) — evaluators/thermal's real 3D-ICE-backed evaluator maps a hierarchy entry with both a `floorplan` block and `attrs.power_w` set onto one 3D-ICE floorplan rectangle; entries missing either are excluded from the modeled die, not an error (a caller may model only the components it has real power figures for). All coordinates are in micrometres (um), matching 3D-ICE's own native unit — see evaluators/thermal/README.md for why this repo doesn't invent a second length unit just for this. `die` (docs/decisions.md D65) is an optional integer, default 0, naming which physical die (in a real, stacked multi-die/chiplet sense) this block sits on — a higher `die` index is physically closer to the heat sink; blocks that share a `die` index are placed on the same physical layer, blocks on different `die` indices are real, separate, thermally-coupled silicon layers, not independent dies evaluated in isolation.

estimator_hints.description: Accelergy-style plug-in keying: which estimator plugin(s) to use for this component, generalised to any cost dimension, not just energy.

interconnect.description: System-level interconnect (NoC/D2D), distinct from per-level 'interconnect' attrs on a hierarchy entry.

noc.description: Free-form by design (existing examples use a descriptive `topology` string like 'mesh_4x4' or 'crossbar' with no further structure — see my-npu-v3.yaml, generic-riscv-soc-v1.yaml). `dimensions`, when present alongside `topology: mesh` or `topology: torus`, describes a real k-ary n-cube network (docs/decisions.md D5): n=2 is a 2D mesh/torus, n=3 is a real 3D NoC (die-stacked, TSV-connected layers) — same topology family, one more dimension. That specific shape maps onto evaluators/booksim's real Booksim2 integration (KNCube network, verified against real 2D and 3D simulations, not assumed); evaluators/booksim raises NotExpressibleError, not a schema error, for a `noc` block that doesn't have it — narrow validation belongs in the adapter, matching every other translator in this repo, not in this shared schema.

dimensions.description: One entry per network dimension, e.g. [8, 8] for a 2D 8x8 mesh, [4, 4, 4] for a 3D 4x4x4 mesh.

routing_function.description: Booksim2 routing function name, e.g. 'dor' (dimension-order routing).

traffic.description: Booksim2 synthetic traffic pattern name, e.g. 'uniform', 'transpose' — see evaluators/booksim/README.md for why traffic is an architecture-level (not workload-level) parameter in v0.1.

chiplet_noc.description: Real chiplet inter-die (D2D) interconnect (docs/decisions.md D66/D67) — a genuinely different network shape from `noc` above, not a variant of it: `noc`'s KNCube family models one uniform, single-die on-chip network; `chiplet_noc` models real, separate per-die networks bridged by explicit D2D links whose latency is caller-declared, not inherited from the in-die default — because a real D2D crossing is a physically different, meaningfully slower link than an in-die wire, and this repo has no clock-frequency concept anywhere to derive a defensible cycle count from a real nanosecond figure (UCIe or otherwise), so it must be declared directly, the same honest-gap posture evaluators/thermal's `attrs.power_w` already established. Any number of dies (each a single crossbar router serving its own declared node count) and any number of D2D links between them (docs/decisions.md D67 generalised D66's own real, deliberately narrow two-die/one-link v0.1) — maps onto Booksim2's real `anynet` topology (an arbitrary router/node connectivity file with real, genuine per-link latency, not a KNCube parameter), verified with real, hand-built two- and three-chiplet anynet simulations before this schema field existed.

latency_cycles.description: The real, physically meaningful part of this block: how many cycles slower a D2D crossing is than the (Booksim2 default, 1-cycle) in-die router-to-node link. Caller-declared, not defaulted — see this block's own top-level description for why.

multi_core.description: Real multi-core/heterogeneous-core system topology (docs/decisions.md D82) — for Stream (docs/decisions.md D80/D81), the first real evaluator here whose own workload/architecture inputs are inherently multi-core, not a single compute array. Each `cores[]` entry's own `architecture` is a genuine, recursive, single-core Flux Architecture IR document (the same narrow single-compute-node shape `evaluators/zigzag`'s own translator already requires) — deliberately not required to declare its own `dram`-class memory level: off-chip access is modelled once, centrally, via `offchip_core_id`, not duplicated per core (the same real convention Stream's own bundled multi-core reference configs use). `core_links` are real point-to-point or shared-bus inter-core bandwidth declarations, distinct from both `noc` (one uniform on-chip network) and `chiplet_noc` (per-die networks bridged by D2D links) — a third, genuinely different real interconnect shape this repo now models.

coordinates.description: 2D placement, Stream's own real `core_coordinates` convention — used for display/provenance only, does not itself affect cost.

architecture.description: A genuine, recursive, single-core Flux Architecture IR document for this core — validated narrowly by the adapter (single compute node, no `dram`-class memory level), not by this shared schema, the same 'schema stays loose, adapter validates narrowly' posture `noc`'s own description above already established.

cores.description: Two entries for a real point-to-point link; more than two for a real shared bus among all listed cores (Stream's own real `type: bus` convention).

offchip_core_id.description: The id of the real, single, shared off-chip DRAM-fronting core every other core reaches through a declared `core_links` entry — Stream's own real bundled off-chip config is reused unmodified for this core (docs/decisions.md D82), the same 'reuse the tool's own real reference, don't fabricate new DRAM-interface detail' posture D74/D78 already established.

constraints.description: Machine-checkable, independent of the cost model — enforced by the validity checker even when the cost model has no opinion (anti-reward-hacking, G14).
